# Chorda voicing knobs (generated by `knobs.py` from `crates/cantus-dsp/src/chorda_voicing.rs`)

A spec is one line `key=value,key=value,…`, applied in order over beta.14's voicing (a later
key overrides an earlier one). "beta.14" is what an empty spec plays; "c16" what candidate 16
(the shipped voicing since `DSP_VERSION` 7) sets, blank where it leaves beta.14's value.

| `reg.<bass\|mid\|treble>.level` | `reg_level[r]` | 0 | (see spec) | Each register's level (dB; bass, middle, treble — `reg.<register>.level`). |
| `draw.<21..108>` | `draws[key-21]` | 0 | (see spec) | Round 40 (candidate 13): each key's draw (0: its own, beta.14's). A key's unison — its strings' detune skew, weights, stiffness and loss scatters, its bridge's resonances — is hashed from the key; a non-zero draw hashes it as another, fixed, so a technician can re-voice one key whose unison landed badly (D#2's flanger) without touching any other. Set by name as `draw.<MIDI key>`. |
| `hf_key.<21..108>` | `hf_keys[key-21]` | 1 | (see spec) | Round 40 (candidate 14): each key's frequency-dependent loss divisor scaled (1: the register's law; < 1 its upper partials die faster) — the reference's middle C loses its partial 9 (~2.4 kHz) 20 dB in 1.5 s, Chorda's under the law ~12 for every unison draw. Set by name as `hf_key.<MIDI key>`. |

Not in a spec: the two tables, `CHORDA_PARTIALS` (each key's partials 2…7, dB, scaled by
`partials_amount`) and `CHORDA_LEVELS` (each key's level, dB, scaled by `levels_amount`) — see SPEC.md.
